newsitem.title: INDIA: Chief of Indian PM's party indicted for corruption.
newsitem.headline: Chief of Indian PM's party indicted for corruption.

text.p: Indian federal police on Monday indicted the head of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party in a $280-million criminal corruption case that has shaken the government only two months into office.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said it indicted Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, and 55 others in the fodder scandal in the state capital, Patna.
Yadav is the first standing state chief minister to be indicted by the federal police agency, authorities said.
CBI officials said the 56 accused were indicted for cheating, forgery, criminal conspiracy and misuse of official authority. The charges carry a maximum penalty of seven years in jail, they said.

Last Friday a junior minister in Gujral's two-month-old government who had been accused in the case resigned. Chandradeo Prasad Varma, who had quit as junior rural areas and employment minister, was among those indicted on Monday.
The case dates back to the 1980s and involves the alleged siphoning off of funds from an animal welfare programme.
Both Yadav, who is president of Gujral's Janata Dal party, and Varma have said they are innocent. Yadav was not immediately available for comment.
Yadav has refused to quit as either Bihar chief minister or Janata Dal president, splitting the prime minister's party ahead of organisational elections due by July 3.
Gujral on Monday reiterated that he believed that Yadav should step down as chief minister, and acknowledged that the scandal was causing trouble for the party.
"It (Janata Dal) is passing through a very difficult time," he told Asian News International in an interview. "It is unable to meet and decide anything."
Left-wing parties in Gujral's 15-party United Front coalition have urged the Bihar chief minister to quit to spare the alliance embarrassment. But he has steadfastly refused.

The main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) pounced on the indictment. "As far as his (Yadav's) continuance as chief minister of Bihar, he does not have the right to do so even for one moment more," BJP spokesman Yashwant Sinha said.
The BJP spokesman, saying Yadav had indicated he would not quit, called on Gujral to dismiss him. "Any delay will further erode the credibility of his government," Sinha said.
But Gujral has been reluctant to recommend to President Shankar Dayal Sharma that he dissolve the Bihar state assembly to bring down Yadav.
Yadav is locked in a party election tussle with challenger Sharad Yadav, no relation of the Bihar chief minister but a key rival in the low-caste Yadav community to which they both belong.
